item.text:
**3B.10 Research Note**

Bottom line: Hasina did not leave Bangladesh safer in 2024. The year ended with a deadly protest crackdown, major civil-unrest deaths and injuries, internet shutdowns, and later reprisals against minorities. There is some narrow positive evidence for Rohingya-related humanitarian protection and border management, but it is indirect, partner-driven, and not enough to offset the overall deterioration.

- [World Report 2025: Bangladesh](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/bangladesh) — Human Rights Watch, 2025. Claim: HRW says 2024 began with mass repression, then escalated into a July crackdown in which nearly 1,000 people, including over 100 children, were reportedly killed, followed by reprisals after Hasina’s ouster and attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities. This is the clearest retrospective evidence that citizens ended the year less safe than they began it. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.7`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh security forces target unarmed students](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/22/bangladesh-security-forces-target-unarmed-students) — Human Rights Watch, July 22, 2024. Claim: HRW reported army deployment, internet shutdowns, and security-force violence against peaceful student protesters, indicating Hasina’s domestic security posture made ordinary citizens less safe, not more safe. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; this shows the year’s central domestic crisis produced a more dangerous and less lawful environment than the one inherited. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024. Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence, a pattern more consistent with fear escalation and blame-shifting than with making citizens safer. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.3`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `2B.6`
- [Bangladesh prime minister Hasina resigns amid mass protests](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/06/bangladesh-prime-minister-hasina-resigns-amid-mass-protests) — Human Rights Watch, August 6, 2024. Claim: HRW described extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and attacks on protesters during the crackdown; the state response clearly increased deaths and injuries rather than reducing them. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Vandalism, Attacks Follow Bangladesh Prime Minister’s Exit](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/08/vandalism-attacks-follow-bangladesh-prime-ministers-exit) — Human Rights Watch, August 8, 2024. Claim: After Hasina’s exit, HRW reported attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities, including torched homes and temples; that means the transition did not leave vulnerable communities safer. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`
- [UN and partners seek $852.4m to support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts](https://www.unhcr.org/news/press-releases/un-and-partners-seek-852-4m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts) — UNHCR, March 13, 2024. Claim: The 2024 Rohingya response plan launched under Bangladeshi authorities targeted women and children and aimed to improve protection, education, livelihoods, and reduce dangerous boat journeys; this is real protection infrastructure, but it is mostly partner-led and does not show Hasina broadly made citizens safer. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.7`, `2B.3`
- [JRP - Joint Response Plan for Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis in Bangladesh - 2024](https://data.unhcr.org/en/documents/details/111224) — UNHCR Data Portal, March 30, 2024. Claim: The 2024 joint response plan targeted Rohingya refugees and vulnerable host communities, including female- or child-headed households, GBV survivors, children at risk, older persons, and persons with disabilities. This is a narrow positive on humanitarian protection, but it is not strong evidence of an overall safer domestic security environment under Hasina. IDs: `3B.10`, `3B.7`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Hasina left Bangladesh broadly safer from political violence, intergroup violence, deaths, injuries, or displacement.
- The strongest positive material is narrow humanitarian assistance for Rohingya and host communities, mostly through UN and partner programs rather than a demonstrated protective state strategy.
- The overall record still points to a net deterioration in civilian safety, especially during the July 2024 crackdown and the post-August violence.
